gaps.lead: I think learning to use a typewriter is a waste of time.
gaps.sentence: I can't ___ how to use a typewriter.
gaps.explanation: 'A waste of time' becomes 'can't see the point in/of doing it'.

gaps.lead: A mechanic repaired my father's roof last week.
gaps.explanation: have something done = arrange for somebody to do it: had his roof repaired.

gaps.lead: Despite his serious injury, he finished the marathon.
If Marc hadn't taken up politics, he might have become a famous art historian.
gaps.sentence: If Marc hadn't taken up politics, he might have ___ himself as an art historian.
gaps.hint: become famous = make a ___ for oneself
gaps.explanation: 'Make a name for himself' means become well known.

gaps.lead: You can only get a seat if you book well in advance.
gaps.explanation: if you don't book = without booking.

gaps.lead: As I get older, I become less patient.
gaps.sentence: The older I get, ___ I become.
gaps.explanation: The older…, the more… — doubled comparatives for parallel change.
